# Example
# And another example

> At the arrival of the rain clouds, ten times the square root of a flock of swans flew to Lake Manasa <term>Manasa</term> <gloss>the sacred Lake Manasarovar in the Himalayas</gloss>. One-eighth of the flock flew away from the water’s edge to a forest of land-lotuses. O young girl, three pairs of swans were seen playing in the water, which was beautiful with young lotus stalks. Tell me the total number of the entire flock.

**Connection of words:** O young girl! At the arrival of the clouds, ten times the square root <note>original: "mula-dashakam," ten times the root</note> of the flock of swans went to Lake Manasa. One-eighth part <term>ashtamshakah</term> <gloss>one-eighth</gloss> flew from the water's edge and went to a forest of land-lotuses. Three pairs of swans were seen playing in water beautiful with young lotus stalks. Therefore, tell the total number of the flock.

**Meaning:** O my dear one, sixteen years of age! <note>The word "Bala" refers to a young girl, often interpreted in this context as sixteen years old.</note> There was a flock of swans. From that group, when the rainy season arrived, ten times the square root of the total went to Lake Manasarovar. One-eighth part of the group flew from the edge of the water to a forest of land-lotuses. Three pairs of swans <note>amounting to six birds</note> were seen playing with great affection in water decorated with soft lotus roots. Say, how many swans were in that group?

**Mathematical Statement:** The root-multiplier <term>mula-gunam</term> is 10. The eighth part is <gloss>1/8</gloss>. The visible quantity <term>drishyam</term> <gloss>the known number of swans not associated with the root or fraction</gloss> is <gloss>6</gloss>. As it was stated that the quantity is "increased or decreased by fractions," we divide the visible quantity and the root-multiplier by the remainder of the fraction <note>calculated as 1 minus 1/8, which is 7/8</note>. This results in an adjusted visible quantity of <gloss>48/7</gloss> and an adjusted root-multiplier of <gloss>80/7</gloss>. Half of the multiplier is <gloss>40/7</gloss>. The square of this is <gloss>1600/49</gloss>. Adding the visible quantity <note>48/7, which is 336/49</note> to this gives <gloss>1936/49</gloss>. The square root of this is <gloss>44/7</gloss>. When this is joined with half the multiplier <gloss>40/7</gloss> and then squared, the resulting flock of swans <term>hansa-rashih</term> is 144.

**Detailed Working:** According to the rule mentioned in the previous verse, we subtract the eighth part <gloss>1/8</gloss> from one. Then <gloss>1/1 - 1/8</gloss> = <gloss>7/8</gloss>. We divide the visible quantity of 6 by this. <gloss>6/1 divided by 7/8</gloss> = <gloss>6/1 × 8/7</gloss> = <gloss>48/7</gloss>. Thus, 48/7 becomes the new visible quantity. Similarly, we divide the root-multiplier of 10 by 7/8. <gloss>10/1 divided by 7/8</gloss> = <gloss>10/1 × 8/7</gloss> = <gloss>80/7</gloss>. Now, taking 48/7 as the visible quantity and 80/7 as the root-multiplier, we perform the operation according to the method in the previous verse. That is, half of the root-multiplier is <gloss>40/7</gloss>. We square this, resulting in <gloss>1600/49</gloss>. We add this to the visible quantity 48/7 in the following way:

<summary>This page presents a mathematical riddle about a flock of swans to demonstrate how to solve a quadratic equation involving square roots. Using a poetic setting of the monsoon and Lake Manasa, it provides the step-by-step algebraic working to find the total population of 144 swans.</summary>
